svg.text: GP-Z1 / Z4 Citrus: zest by a force-limited rasp, peel by depth-shoe paring
Force sets the zest depth, a shoe sets the paring depth — neither needs a camera.
Z1 zest: conf. H · Z4 pare: M
GP-Z1 Zest: spin against a fine rasp
force-limited, one pass: it cannot reach the white pith
GP-Z4 Peeled orange: pare to the flesh
the onion blade-and-shoe, 5–6 mm proud, on the turning fruit
curved photo-etched rasp traverses pole to pole once
20–30 % clings to the rasp: rinsed off with the recipe’s own liquid
top and tail cut first; the top face shows the peel thickness

g.text: blade 5–6 mm proud of the shoe
1/6 Zest: the lemon turns on a two-prong spit at 60 rpm.
2/6 A curved fine rasp presses on with only 2–4 N and travels once from pole to pole.
3/6 Each pass takes 0.3–0.5 mm of the 1–2 mm zest layer, so the bitter pith is never reached.
4/6 Peeled orange: top and tail are cut off; the fruit turns on the spit.
5/6 The shoe rides on the peel; the blade 5–6 mm proud cuts peel and pith away in one traverse.
6/6 The bare fruit is sliced into rounds.
